Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Liam / FinSecure team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the thorough discussion. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we have a shared view: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- No customer raw data stored outside your environment (FinSecure VPC) unless explicitly allowed.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption keys.
- Audit logs (access, admin actions, model inputs/outputs metadata) forwarded to your SIEM.
- SOC 2 compliance and evidence for controls around access, logging, retention.
- Data residency: US (primary region: us-east-1).

Deployment options we discussed (high level):
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for FinSecure with tenant isolation at the runtime layer. Typically faster to stand up (2-3 weeks) and supports strict RBAC, encryption at rest, and per-tenant logging. Network path routes through a Redwood-managed VPC (we can restrict egress and logging).
- Private VPC (VPC peering or on-prem package): customer-managed network connectivity where the inference runtime is deployed inside your VPC or peered to it. Supports customer KMS, full control over networking, and no outbound data retention by Redwood. Longer setup (4-6 weeks typical) but aligns best with the "no data leaves our VPC" requirement.

Clarifying questions to confirm before we propose a formal SOW/POC:
1) When you say "no raw data leaves our VPC", does that also require that model inputs/outputs metadata (headers, timestamps) never transit Redwood-managed storage?
2) Is customer-managed KMS/HSM mandatory for all workloads, or only for production/pci/sensitive workloads?
3) Are there any regulatory residency constraints beyond US (e.g., EU backups)?
4) Do you have a preferred method for audit log ingestion (syslog, S3 push, Splunk/Datadog forwarder)?

Attachments: Redwood-Private-vs-Dedicated-one-pager.pdf, Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf (attached for checklist items).

Recommended next steps:
- If your primary blocker is data not leaving your VPC, we recommend piloting Private VPC.
- If you want faster time-to-value and can accept restricted egress controls, we can pilot Dedicated capacity and then migrate to Private VPC for production.

Proposed cadence: technical kickoff next week to map networking/KMS, followed by a 2-4 week pilot depending on option chosen.

Can you confirm answers to the questions above and share the security questionnaire (if you have one)? I can then pull in our infrastructure team and Neha (cc'd) to scope the technical work.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Quick answers to your questions:
1) "No raw data leaves our VPC" means raw inputs/outputs (full payloads) must not be persisted or accessible outside our VPC. Metadata (timestamps, non-sensitive headers) is OK to flow to Redwood for observability but we'd prefer to keep that minimal.
2) Customer-managed KMS is mandatory for production workloads handling PII/payment data. For non-prod we can use Redwood-managed keys during evaluation.
3) Residency: US-only for production. Development/test can be in other regions.
4) Preferred log ingestion: Splunk forwarder (we'll provide endpoint), but we can do S3 push if easier on your side.

We do have a standard security questionnaire — attaching that now. Our security team will need to review your SOC 2 evidence and network architecture.

Preferred path: Private VPC for production. However, we are open to a short Dedicated pilot if you can guarantee no persistence outside our VPC and provide documented controls. Can you provide ballpark timelines and cost ranges for both paths? Also, are there maintenance windows or expected downtime for Private VPC upgrades?

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Ops | FinSecure
liam.oconnor@finsecure.com

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the questionnaire. Short answers + what we need from you to move toward a Private VPC pilot: 

1) Private VPC behavior:
- When deployed in Private VPC mode (peered or customer-managed), Redwood's inference runtime runs in your VPC or a tightly peered subnet. We do not persist raw inputs/outputs to Redwood-managed object storage by default. Any telemetry we keep is configurable and can be limited to non-sensitive metadata.

2) KMS/HSM:
- We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMKs) for data-at-rest encryption of model artifacts, logs, and any persisted caches. HSM integrations are supported via BYOK workflows — we'll provide the onboarding steps.

3) Audit logs & SIEM:
- We can forward logs over syslog/Splunk forwarder or S3 push. For Splunk, we'll need the endpoint and a shared token/certificate.

4) Timeline & cost (ballpark):
- Dedicated pilot: 2-3 weeks to stand up + cost ~ $5k–$12k/month depending on capacity (pilot size).
- Private VPC pilot: 4-6 weeks initial onboarding + one-time onboarding engineering fee ($25k–$40k depending on custom peering/on-prem work) and running costs dependent on reserved capacity. Exact pricing depends on instance types and retention policies; we can provide a formal estimate once we know desired concurrency and retention.

5) Maintenance windows:
- Private VPC: normal minor upgrades can be done with rolling updates and no customer-visible downtime for inference traffic if we coordinate maintenance windows; major upgrades may require short maintenance windows (we'll schedule with you).

What we need from FinSecure to scope a pilot:
- Completed security questionnaire (thanks for sending).
- Desired pilot scope (number of concurrent requests, typical sequence lengths, latency SLOs).
- Splunk endpoint details or S3 bucket for logs.
- Confirmation if customer KMS is required for the pilot or only for production.

Next steps I'd propose:
- Mateo/Neha: technical kickoff (30-60m) this week to map network & KMS requirements.
- Security team: review SOC 2 summary (attached) and we'll follow up with detailed evidence.
- Commercial: I'll prepare a scoped SOW for Private VPC and a short-term Dedicated pilot option so you can choose which path to accelerate.

Attaching: VPC-onboarding-checklist.pdf (checklist we use for Private VPC onboarding).

If that sounds good I'll put together calendar invites.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
